intent.raw_query: Vietnam on $800, backpacking 10 days, street food and culture, April 2026

experiences.name: Hanoi Old Quarter Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Wander through the maze-like streets of Hanoi's Old Quarter sampling iconic Vietnamese street food including Bun Cha, Banh Mi, Pho, and Egg Coffee. Join a local-led walking tour or explore independently through the 36 guild streets, stopping at hole-in-the-wall stalls packed with locals.

experiences.name: Hoi An Ancient Town Lantern Festival
experiences.description: Experience the magical monthly lantern festival in the UNESCO-listed Ancient Town of Hoi An. Release a lantern on the Thu Bon River, explore centuries-old merchant houses, visit Japanese covered bridges, and feast on local specialties like Cao Lau and White Rose dumplings at riverside market stalls.

experiences.name: Motorbike Ride on the Hai Van Pass
experiences.description: Rent a motorbike and conquer the legendary Hai Van Pass, one of Southeast Asia's most scenic mountain roads stretching between Da Nang and Hue. Enjoy breathtaking coastal views, stop at old French and American war bunkers, and feel the ultimate backpacker freedom on this iconic route.
experiences.location: Hai Van Pass, between Da Nang and Hue

experiences.name: Mekong Delta Boat Tour and Local Market Visit
experiences.description: Take a budget boat tour through the lush waterways of the Mekong Delta from Can Tho. Visit the famous Cai Rang floating market at dawn where vendors sell tropical fruits and local produce from their boats, sample fresh coconut candy, and cycle through riverside villages for an authentic rural Vietnamese cultural experience.
experiences.location: Cai Rang Floating Market, Can Tho

experiences.name: Banh Mi and Pho Cooking Class in Hue
experiences.description: Join an affordable hands-on cooking class in Vietnam's imperial city of Hue, learning to prepare regional specialties like Bun Bo Hue (spicy beef noodle soup) and Banh Khoai (crispy pancakes). Visit a local wet market with your instructor to source fresh ingredients and gain deep insight into Vietnamese culinary traditions and imperial court cuisine.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Vietnam
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities - flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and prepare for arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at 13:00, clear customs and immigration, collect baggage. Take a budget airport bus or shared shuttle to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and take a slow walk along the beachfront to get oriented with the local area. Explore the nearby streets on foot.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll the local night market or beachside promenade near the resort. Pick up a local SIM card at a convenience store for cheap data. Explore the neighborhood streets and soak in the Vietnamese atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a quick snack at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and cheap bowl of Pho or Banh Mi from a street stall near the airport or on the way to the resort (under $2 USD).
meals.dinner: Find a local com tam (broken rice) stall near the resort for a hearty budget dinner with grilled pork, egg, and pickled vegetables for around $2-3 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is light due to afternoon arrival. Focus on settling in, getting a local SIM card, and exchanging currency at a local bank or ATM for the best rates. Avoid airport exchange counters.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and head to the nearest local market (cho) to experience the morning hustle. Watch vendors sell fresh produce, seafood, and street food. Try a bowl of Bun Bo Hue or Banh Canh at a market stall for breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local beach area and nearby cultural landmarks such as a local pagoda or temple within walking or cycling distance. Rent a bicycle for the day (around $3-5 USD) to cover more ground cheaply. Visit any nearby fishing village to see traditional Vietnamese coastal life.
day_by_day.evening: Head to a local beachside area for sunset views. Join backpackers at a budget-friendly bar or grab cheap cold Bia Hoi (draft beer, around $0.50 USD) at a street-side stall. Explore the night food scene.

meals.breakfast: Bowl of Bun Bo Hue or Banh Canh at the local morning market for $1-2 USD.
meals.lunch: Banh Mi sandwich from a street cart near the beach for $1-1.50 USD.
meals.dinner: Grilled seafood skewers and fresh spring rolls from a beachside street food stall for $4-6 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Renting a bicycle is one of the best budget ways to explore Vietnamese towns. Always negotiate the rental price. Carry a small backpack with water and sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a nearby historic or cultural site such as a local museum, communal house (dinh), or ancient temple. Many such sites have free or very low entry fees (under $1 USD). Arrive early to beat the heat and crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a budget local bus or xe om (motorbike taxi) to explore a nearby town or village. Walk through the old quarter streets, browse local handicraft shops without buying, and observe daily Vietnamese life. Try street-side coconut coffee.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area and explore the local street food scene. Look for a busy local restaurant with plastic stools on the sidewalk — a sign of authentic and affordable food.

meals.breakfast: Xoi (sticky rice with toppings) from a street vendor for $1 USD.
meals.lunch: Com Binh Dan (everyday rice dish with multiple side dishes) at a local canteen for $2-3 USD.
meals.dinner: Hu Tieu noodle soup or Mi Quang at a local pho shop for $2-3 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Always carry small denominations of Vietnamese Dong for street food purchases. Most street stalls do not accept cards. Bargain politely at local shops but not at food stalls.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning walk along the beach at sunrise — free and incredibly scenic. Join local Vietnamese doing morning exercises or Tai Chi on the beach. Explore the shoreline and look for local fishermen returning with their catch.
day_by_day.afternoon: Organize a budget day trip to a nearby natural attraction such as sand dunes, a waterfall, or a national park depending on the exact resort location. Join a group tour from a local travel agency for the cheapest rate (around $10-15 USD for a group tour).
day_by_day.evening: Cook or assemble your own meal by shopping at the local market for fresh fruit, snacks, and drinks. Spend the evening socializing with fellow backpackers at the hostel common area or a cheap beachside bar.

meals.breakfast: Banh Cuon (steamed rice rolls) or Pho from a nearby breakfast stall for $1.50 USD.
meals.lunch: Pack a Banh Mi or buy fresh fruit and snacks from the market for a picnic-style lunch during the day trip — under $3 USD.
meals.dinner: Self-assembled meal from the local market: fresh fruit, spring rolls, and a cold drink for $3-4 USD total.

day_by_day.notes: When booking day trips, always compare prices at multiple travel agencies on the same street. Group tours are significantly cheaper than private tours. Confirm what is included (entrance fees, lunch, transport).

day_by_day.morning: Explore a local craft village or artisan workshop nearby. Many Vietnamese towns have villages specializing in pottery, weaving, or lacquerware. Entrance is usually free and you can watch artisans at work.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local pagoda complex for cultural immersion. Dress respectfully (cover shoulders and knees). Spend time observing Buddhist rituals and architecture. Walk the surrounding garden grounds.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the busiest street food area in the nearest town. Try multiple small dishes from different vendors — this is the backpacker way of eating in Vietnam. Sample Goi Cuon (fresh rolls), Nem (fried spring rolls), and Che (sweet dessert soup).

meals.breakfast: Ca Phe Trung (Vietnamese egg coffee) and a sweet pastry from a local cafe for $1.50-2 USD.
meals.lunch: Bun Cha (grilled pork with noodles) at a local lunch spot for $2-3 USD.
meals.dinner: Street food crawl — spend $5-7 USD total across 3-4 different street vendors for a variety of small dishes and snacks.

day_by_day.notes: Vietnamese egg coffee is a must-try unique experience. Look for family-run cafes rather than tourist-oriented ones for the most authentic and affordable cup. Pagodas are free but small donations are appreciated.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget overnight or early morning bus to a nearby major destination (e.g., Hoi An, Da Nang, Nha Trang, or Hue depending on resort location). Book open-tour sleeper buses through local agencies for $5-10 USD. Depart early to maximize time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at the new destination and check into a budget guesthouse or hostel dorm (around $5-8 USD per night). Drop your bags and immediately explore the old town or city center on foot. Walk the main streets and get oriented.
day_by_day.evening: Join a free walking tour if available (tip-based) or explore the night market. Try the local specialty dish of whatever city you are visiting.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the bus or grab a quick Banh Mi before departure for $1 USD.
meals.lunch: Cao Lau (Hoi An noodles) or local specialty at the new destination for $2-3 USD.
meals.dinner: White Rose dumplings and Banh Xeo (sizzling crepe) at a local eatery for $3-5 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Sleeper buses are the most budget-friendly way to travel between Vietnamese cities. Book 1-2 days in advance through your guesthouse or a local agency. Keep valuables in your daypack during bus travel.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the old town or historic district of the city you traveled to. Walk through ancient streets, visit heritage houses (small entry fee of $1-2 USD), and browse the local market. Take photos of colorful lanterns, temples, and colonial architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle (around $2-3 USD for the day) to explore the outskirts of the city. Visit a local beach, rice paddy fields, or a nearby village. Cycling is the quintessential backpacker way to explore Vietnamese towns.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the old town for the evening lantern lighting (if in Hoi An) or the night market. Enjoy cheap street food and cold drinks. Buy a handmade souvenir if budget allows.

meals.breakfast: Mi Quang (turmeric noodles) at a local market stall for $1.50 USD.
meals.lunch: Com Ga (chicken rice) at a popular local lunch spot for $2 USD.
meals.dinner: Banh Mi Phuong or equivalent famous local sandwich shop for $1.50 USD, plus a bowl of sweet Che dessert for $0.50 USD.

day_by_day.notes: In Hoi An, the combined heritage ticket covers multiple historic houses and is worth it at around $5 USD. Avoid tourist restaurants on the main strip — walk one or two streets back for half the price and better food.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget day trip to a nearby natural or cultural attraction such as the Marble Mountains, My Son Sanctuary, or a local beach depending on your location. Book through a local guesthouse for the best group rates.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the day trip or return and explore a local cooking class. Many budget cooking classes in Vietnam cost $15-20 USD and include a market tour, cooking session, and lunch — great cultural value.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the guesthouse or hostel common area. Share travel tips with fellow backpackers. Plan the next leg of the journey. Explore a local bar for cheap Bia Hoi.

meals.breakfast: Pho Bo (beef noodle soup) at a street stall near the guesthouse for $1.50-2 USD.
meals.lunch: Included in the cooking class or day trip, or grab a Banh Mi for $1 USD.
meals.dinner: Bun Thit Nuong (grilled pork with cold noodles) at a local eatery for $2-3 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Cooking classes are one of the best budget cultural experiences in Vietnam. You learn to cook, eat well, and take recipes home. Always check reviews and compare prices — many classes are competitively priced.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a sunrise visit to a local landmark, temple, or viewpoint. Sunrise visits are free and the best time for photography with soft light and fewer tourists. Grab a street-side ca phe sua da (iced milk coffee) to start the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon doing a final deep exploration of the local area. Visit any remaining sites on your list. Shop for budget souvenirs at the local market — lacquerware, silk scarves, and handmade crafts are good value. Bargain respectfully.
day_by_day.evening: Take a budget overnight sleeper bus or train back toward the resort area or to the next destination. Pack light snacks and water for the journey.

meals.breakfast: Ca Phe Sua Da and a Banh Mi from a street cart for $1.50 USD total.
meals.lunch: Final meal at a favorite local spot discovered during the trip — splurge slightly with a $4-5 USD meal.
meals.dinner: Pack snacks from the market for the overnight bus: fresh fruit, crackers, and a cold drink for $2-3 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Book your return sleeper bus or train at least one day in advance. Keep your main backpack in the bus luggage compartment and carry a small daypack with valuables, snacks, and a layer for the cold AC on the bus.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive back at or near the resort area in the morning after the overnight bus. Check back in or freshen up. Take a final relaxed morning walk along the beach or through the local neighborhood. Reflect on the journey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the last afternoon revisiting a favorite local spot, trying any street food you missed, or simply relaxing at the beachfront. Visit a local cafe for a long, slow Vietnamese coffee and write in a travel journal.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Vietnam — treat yourself to a slightly nicer local seafood dinner (still budget-friendly at $8-12 USD). Watch the sunset over the beach. Pack your bags and prepare for departure. Exchange any leftover Dong back to your home currency.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the bus or grab Xoi or Banh Cuon upon arrival for $1-1.50 USD.
meals.lunch: Com Tam with extra toppings as a farewell meal for $3-4 USD.
meals.dinner: Grilled fresh seafood at a local beachside restaurant as a final Vietnam splurge — $8-12 USD for a full meal with drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Keep enough Dong for your final meals, transport to the airport, and any departure taxes. Spend remaining small change on snacks or drinks at the airport. Vietnam is incredibly affordable — even a splurge dinner on the last night fits comfortably within a backpacker budget. Safe travels!

trip_options.title: Classic Vietnam Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and transit time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at 13:00, clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll along the beachfront to get oriented with the surroundings.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the nearest local night market or beachside promenade. Sample introductory Vietnamese street food snacks like bánh mì and fresh spring rolls from nearby stalls.

meals.breakfast: On the flight
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bowl of phở or bún bò Huế from a local street stall near the resort after check-in (~50,000–80,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Beachside local restaurant near the resort — try grilled seafood platters and Vietnamese iced tea (~150,000–250,000 VND per person)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Exchange some currency at the airport or a local bank for better rates. Purchase a local SIM card at the airport for easy navigation.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a sunrise beach walk along the resort's beachfront. Rent a bicycle from the resort or a nearby shop and cycle through the local fishing village to observe morning life and fishermen returning with their catch.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby cultural landmark or pagoda in the local area. Explore the town's old quarter or central market to browse local handicrafts, spices, and fresh produce.
day_by_day.evening: Join a street food walking tour in the nearest town center. Try local specialties such as cao lầu, white rose dumplings, or bánh xèo (Vietnamese sizzling pancakes).

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or a local bánh mì sandwich from a street cart (~30,000–50,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood at a local market eatery — grilled fish with rice (~80,000–120,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Street food tour dinner — mix of small dishes from various stalls (~100,000–180,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes. Bring sunscreen and a hat as April can be warm. Bargain politely at local markets.

day_by_day.morning: Take a half-day cooking class at a local culinary school. Learn to prepare 3–4 traditional Vietnamese dishes including fresh herbs selection, pho broth preparation, and spring roll wrapping.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby historical museum or cultural center to understand the region's history and heritage. Browse local art galleries or craft workshops.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Vietnamese water puppet show or live folk music performance at a cultural venue nearby.

meals.breakfast: Included light breakfast before the cooking class
meals.lunch: Eat what you cooked in the cooking class — a full Vietnamese meal (~included in class fee of 300,000–500,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Mid-range restaurant with outdoor seating — try cơm tấm (broken rice with grilled pork) and fresh coconut (~120,000–200,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class in advance online or through the resort concierge. Cultural shows typically start at 18:00–19:00, book tickets early.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to a nearby UNESCO World Heritage Site or natural landmark (e.g., ancient town, national park, or cave system depending on exact resort location). Depart early by local bus or hired motorbike taxi.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the heritage site — walk through ancient streets, temples, and gardens. Hire a local guide for deeper cultural context (~100,000–150,000 VND for 2 hours).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area by early evening. Relax at a rooftop bar or beachfront café with sunset views and local craft beer or fresh fruit smoothies.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort or grab sticky rice (xôi) from a street vendor (~20,000–40,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Local restaurant at the heritage site — set lunch menu with regional specialties (~100,000–150,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Beachfront seafood BBQ restaurant — choose your fresh catch and have it grilled to order (~200,000–300,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly when visiting temples and pagodas — cover shoulders and knees. Carry a reusable water bottle to stay hydrated.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a motorbike or join a guided scooter tour to explore the countryside surrounding the resort. Ride through rice paddies, local villages, and scenic coastal roads.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at a local artisan village — observe traditional crafts like lantern-making, silk weaving, or pottery. Try your hand at one of the crafts in a short workshop.
day_by_day.evening: Return to town and explore a vibrant local night market. Shop for souvenirs, street snacks, and handmade goods.

meals.breakfast: Pho or bún bò from a neighborhood street stall (~40,000–70,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Roadside village eatery during the countryside ride — simple rice and vegetable dishes (~60,000–100,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Night market food crawl — banh mi, grilled corn, chè (Vietnamese sweet dessert soup), and fresh sugarcane juice (~80,000–150,000 VND total)

day_by_day.notes: Ensure you have a valid international driving permit if renting a motorbike. Alternatively, hire a local driver for safety. Helmets are mandatory.

day_by_day.morning: Relax morning — swim in the sea or resort pool. Optional: take a yoga or tai chi class on the beach if offered by the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Boat trip to nearby islands or a river cruise to explore local waterways, mangroves, and floating villages. Snorkeling optional if equipment is available.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a beachfront bar. Attend a local cultural event or live music session at a nearby venue.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast — enjoy fresh tropical fruits, Vietnamese rice porridge (cháo), and strong Vietnamese drip coffee
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the boat or island — fresh tropical fruits, sandwiches, and coconut water (~included in boat tour or ~80,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Upscale local restaurant — splurge slightly on a set menu featuring regional specialties and Vietnamese wine (~300,000–400,000 VND per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the boat trip through the resort or a reputable local tour operator. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a hat, and a light jacket for the boat.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local Buddhist temple or Cham tower complex for a peaceful morning of cultural exploration. Observe morning prayers and interact respectfully with monks if permitted.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a local street food market — take your time sampling regional snacks like bánh căn, nem lụi, or mì Quảng (regional noodle dishes). Chat with vendors about their recipes.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a community cultural event, lantern festival, or traditional ceremony if available. Walk the lantern-lit streets and enjoy the atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Vietnamese drip coffee and bánh cuốn (steamed rice rolls) from a local breakfast spot (~40,000–60,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Street food market feast — try 3–4 different dishes from different stalls (~100,000–160,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Cozy mid-range Vietnamese restaurant — lẩu (hot pot) shared meal with vegetables, tofu, and meat (~150,000–250,000 VND per person)

day_by_day.notes: Remove shoes before entering temples. Speak quietly and avoid loud behavior in religious sites. Photography is usually allowed but always ask first.

day_by_day.morning: Take a guided hiking or trekking excursion to a nearby hill, nature reserve, or viewpoint. Enjoy panoramic views of the coastline and surrounding landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local coffee plantation or tea farm if available in the region. Learn about Vietnam's world-renowned coffee culture and try a tasting session including cà phê trứng (egg coffee) or weasel coffee.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the resort. Optional: get a traditional Vietnamese massage at a local spa (~200,000–350,000 VND for 60 minutes).

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast — fruit, yogurt, and Vietnamese coffee before the hike
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch during the trek or at the plantation café (~80,000–120,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant or nearby mid-range eatery — try chả cá (turmeric fish with dill) or bò lúc lắc (shaking beef) (~180,000–280,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy footwear for hiking. Bring insect repellent and a light rain jacket. Start the hike early to avoid peak afternoon heat.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning exploring a lesser-known local neighborhood on foot — wander through alleyways, observe daily life, visit a local school or community center if welcomed.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local museum dedicated to Vietnamese history, war history, or ethnic minority cultures. Spend 2–3 hours absorbing the exhibits and context.
day_by_day.evening: Final big dinner at a highly-rated local restaurant — celebrate the trip with a full Vietnamese feast. Try dishes you haven't had yet such as bún chả, gỏi cuốn, or bánh khoái.

meals.breakfast: Street-side breakfast — xôi (sticky rice with toppings) and iced Vietnamese coffee (~40,000–60,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Simple local eatery near the museum — cơm bình dân (budget rice plate with multiple sides) (~60,000–90,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at a well-reviewed local restaurant — multi-course Vietnamese meal with fresh beer (bia hơi) (~300,000–450,000 VND per person)

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to pick up any remaining souvenirs. Check museum opening hours in advance as some close on Mondays. Tip generously at restaurants if service was excellent.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise beach walk or swim. Pack bags and complete resort checkout formalities. Leave a review for the resort if you enjoyed your stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute exploration of the local area — revisit a favorite spot, grab final street food snacks, and pick up any forgotten souvenirs or local products (Vietnamese coffee, spices, silk items).
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to the airport or next destination. Reflect on the journey — 10 days of Vietnamese culture, street food, and adventure.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast or a beloved street stall — enjoy one last bowl of phở (~40,000–70,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Light meal near the resort or airport area — bánh mì sandwich and fresh juice (~50,000–80,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Airport meal or dinner at destination if continuing travel

day_by_day.notes: Check flight details and arrive at the airport at least 2–3 hours before departure. Declare any food items when passing through customs. Keep some VND for airport snacks and tips.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Vietnam Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at the airport, clear immigration and customs, meet private transfer driver. Enjoy a scenic luxury transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, unwind with a welcome drink, and explore the beachfront resort grounds and private beach area.
day_by_day.evening: Gentle sunset stroll along the beachfront. Enjoy a relaxed first evening at the resort's signature restaurant with panoramic ocean views. Early night to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: On the flight
meals.lunch: Light snack or airport lounge meal on arrival
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort signature restaurant - fresh Vietnamese seafood tasting menu with locally sourced ingredients and fine wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Request early check-in if available. Confirm transfer with resort concierge before landing. Keep Day 1 light to recover from long-haul Lufthansa flight.

day_by_day.morning: Indulge in a lavish resort breakfast with ocean views. Join a guided cultural orientation walk through the nearest local village with a private guide - explore traditional Vietnamese architecture, temples, and morning market activity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private street food tour of the local town with a renowned food guide. Sample iconic Vietnamese dishes including bánh mì, phở, fresh spring rolls, and local specialties at carefully vetted street stalls and hidden gems.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort for a sunset cocktail at the beach bar. Enjoy a premium Vietnamese fine dining experience at a top-rated local restaurant featuring elevated traditional cuisine with modern presentation.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast buffet with made-to-order Vietnamese and international options
meals.lunch: Street food tour - curated tastings across 6-8 local vendors (included in tour)
meals.dinner: Upscale Vietnamese restaurant - multi-course tasting menu featuring regional specialties with sommelier-selected wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Book private street food tour in advance through concierge. Wear comfortable walking shoes. Carry light cash for street food vendors.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning private yoga session on the beach at sunrise. Followed by a traditional Vietnamese cooking class at a premium culinary school - learn to prepare pho, banh xeo, and fresh herbs dishes from a master chef.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private boat charter to explore nearby coastal areas, hidden coves, or local fishing villages. Snorkeling or kayaking in crystal-clear waters with premium equipment provided.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort for a luxury spa treatment - traditional Vietnamese herbal massage or hot stone therapy. Sunset dinner at a cliffside or waterfront restaurant with premium seafood.

meals.breakfast: Light healthy breakfast at resort before yoga
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes prepared during your cooking class with the chef and fellow guests
meals.dinner: Waterfront fine dining restaurant - grilled lobster, tiger prawns, and fresh catch of the day with chilled Sancerre

day_by_day.notes: Book spa treatments and boat charter 24 hours in advance. Cooking class typically runs 3-4 hours. Bring reef-safe sunscreen for the boat trip.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided excursion to a nearby UNESCO World Heritage Site or significant cultural landmark (such as ancient temples, imperial citadels, or historic old towns depending on resort location). Explore with an expert historian guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue cultural exploration with a visit to local artisan workshops - witness traditional lacquerware, silk weaving, or pottery making. Purchase premium handcrafted souvenirs directly from master craftspeople.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Vietnamese water puppet show or cultural performance. Dinner at an acclaimed restaurant known for preserving authentic regional recipes.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Premium lunch at a heritage restaurant near the cultural site - try bún bò Huế or cao lầu depending on region
meals.dinner: Award-winning Vietnamese restaurant - royal cuisine tasting menu inspired by imperial court recipes

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly for temple visits - cover shoulders and knees. Hire a licensed cultural guide for the deepest experience. Book evening cultural show tickets in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise photography walk through local rice paddies, fishing harbors, or scenic landscapes with a professional photographer guide. Capture authentic Vietnamese rural life in golden morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Luxury day trip to explore a nearby natural wonder - limestone karst formations, national park, or river delta by private speedboat or seaplane depending on location.
day_by_day.evening: Romantic beachside private dining setup at the resort - personalized menu prepared by the executive chef with candles, flowers, and ocean soundtrack.

meals.breakfast: Grab-and-go premium picnic breakfast prepared by resort for the sunrise walk
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch on the boat or at a scenic viewpoint - charcuterie, fresh tropical fruits, Vietnamese sandwiches, champagne
meals.dinner: Private beach dinner at resort - 5-course personalized tasting menu with premium wine pairing and live acoustic Vietnamese music

day_by_day.notes: Photography tour requires early 5:00-5:30 AM departure. Coordinate private beach dinner setup with concierge 48 hours in advance. This is an ideal evening for a special occasion celebration.

day_by_day.morning: Immersive market experience - visit a bustling local wet market at peak morning hours with a private chef guide. Learn to select the freshest ingredients, interact with vendors, and understand Vietnamese food culture at its roots.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby national museum or cultural heritage center to understand Vietnam's rich history, the influence of various dynasties, and the country's journey through the 20th century. Private guided tour included.
day_by_day.evening: Rooftop bar experience at a premier hotel in the nearest city for panoramic views and craft cocktails. Follow with dinner at a Michelin-recommended or James Beard-recognized Vietnamese restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Light resort breakfast before market visit
meals.lunch: Chef-guided lunch at a beloved local eatery near the market - authentic pho or bun bo with premium toppings
meals.dinner: Michelin-starred or top-rated Vietnamese fine dining - innovative modern Vietnamese cuisine with French-Vietnamese fusion influences

day_by_day.notes: Market visit is best between 6:00-9:00 AM. Wear comfortable shoes for cobblestone streets. Keep an open mind at the wet market - it is a raw, authentic cultural experience.

day_by_day.morning: Full morning of leisure at the resort - enjoy the infinity pool, private beach, or a second spa treatment. Optional: stand-up paddleboarding or windsurfing lesson with resort instructors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private cyclo or vintage Vespa tour through charming local streets, French colonial architecture, and hidden alleyways with a knowledgeable local guide. Stop at boutique galleries and artisan shops.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise on a traditional wooden junk boat or luxury catamaran with cocktails, canapés, and live music. Return for a late dinner at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Champagne brunch at the resort poolside restaurant
meals.lunch: Trendy café lunch during the Vespa tour - avocado toast meets Vietnamese bánh mì, egg coffee, and fresh coconut
meals.dinner: Resort's premium beachfront restaurant - whole grilled fish, seafood hot pot, and seasonal Vietnamese desserts

day_by_day.notes: Vespa tour helmets are mandatory - ensure guide provides certified safety gear. Sunset cruise timing depends on sunset hour - check with concierge. Book in advance as cruises fill quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to a nearby island or coastal destination by private speedboat or helicopter transfer. Explore pristine beaches, coral reefs, and untouched natural landscapes inaccessible to mass tourists.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue island exploration with snorkeling, diving, or a guided jungle trek to a waterfall or panoramic viewpoint. Enjoy complete seclusion and natural beauty.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort. Enjoy a traditional Vietnamese herbal bath ritual followed by a four-hand massage at the resort spa. Light, healthy dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Luxury island picnic or beachside BBQ with fresh seafood, tropical fruits, and chilled rosé wine
meals.dinner: Light and healthy dinner at resort wellness restaurant - Vietnamese herb salads, steamed fish, and detox juices

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter transfer adds premium cost but saves time - confirm availability with concierge. Bring waterproof bags for electronics on the boat. Apply sunscreen generously for full-day outdoor activity.

day_by_day.morning: Final immersive cultural experience - attend a traditional Vietnamese tea ceremony or participate in a Buddhist temple morning ritual with monks. Meditative and deeply authentic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Premium shopping excursion to local boutiques, silk shops, and high-end Vietnamese designer stores. Purchase bespoke ao dai (traditional Vietnamese dress), custom tailored clothing, or premium lacquerware art pieces.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell gala dinner at the resort's best restaurant - chef's special menu celebrating the best of Vietnamese cuisine across all regions, with premium wine and spirits. Live traditional music performance.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Vietnamese breakfast at a local café near the temple - xôi (sticky rice), bánh cuốn, and Vietnamese iced coffee
meals.lunch: Elegant lunch at a boutique restaurant in the shopping district - contemporary Vietnamese cuisine with artistic plating
meals.dinner: Grand farewell tasting dinner at resort - 7-course Vietnamese culinary journey from North to South with premium beverage pairing

day_by_day.notes: Temple visit requires modest dress and respectful behavior. For custom tailoring, visit the tailor on Day 6 or 7 to allow 2-3 days for completion. Farewell dinner reservation should be made at least 3 days in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk on the private beach. Mindful reflection and photography of the resort surroundings. Last resort breakfast with ocean views. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Late checkout if flight allows. Final dip in the infinity pool or a last indulgent spa treatment. Resort concierge arranges luxury private transfer to the airport with ample time for check-in.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Vietnam. If evening flight, enjoy the airport lounge with premium amenities before boarding.

meals.breakfast: Grand final resort breakfast - order everything you loved during the stay
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at the resort or airport lounge depending on flight time
meals.dinner: Airport business/first class lounge dining or onboard meal on Lufthansa return flight

day_by_day.notes: Confirm late checkout with resort at least 48 hours in advance (typically available until 16:00 for premium guests). Allow minimum 3 hours before international departure for airport procedures. Keep a small amount of Vietnamese dong for last-minute purchases at the airport.

query: Vietnam on $800, backpacking 10 days, street food and culture, April 2026
